chunks: From him, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Abbas, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who threw the pebbles (at the Jamarat) while he was riding, and he said: There is no objection (it is permissible).

key_terms.رَمَى الْجِمَارَ: Stoning the Jamarat (ritual throwing of pebbles)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to throw pebbles at the Jamarat while riding a camel or horse during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the permissibility of stoning the Jamarat while mounted, reflecting the jurisprudential principle of *rukhas* (dispensations) for those facing physical difficulty or fatigue during Hajj. This ruling underscores the flexibility within Shia fiqh to accommodate the varying capacities of pilgrims, ensuring the ritual remains accessible without compromising its validity.
